priorFindings.assessment: Selected ordinary C6 no longer restores at incoming Stop. Original SDK close completion waits within the existing finite observer budget for original revActive settlement, restores descriptors, emits event6 and drains scalar acknowledgements before returning to child finish/exit. The timeout path therefore reaches the restoration seam without a fabricated Stop; cancellation retains later-entry observation through native settlement and original close.

Actual callback and diagnostic/stderr surfaces are privately scanned before content checks. New assertion actuals are only scalar booleans/counts, identity checks are scalar, and diagnostic parsing failures are replaced by a fixed sanitized assertion without the original cause.

Guided stop fulfillment and rejection both now invoke the selected retry task after busy settles. Busy-timeout or failed descriptor restoration retains the task and runtime tag. However, the Java caller skips the command that invokes this retained task on the unconfirmed-cleanup branch; see remaining findings.

findings.title: Legacy revocation completion blocks C6 cleanup before seal/restoration retry
findings.sourceEvidence: p8C6Run reaches p3CleanupOwnedResources before the C6 completion helper. That shared cleanup still calls p4AwaitRevocationObserverCompletion before sending the producer seal. Its unchanged completion predicate requires residualSettlements==1, residualFulfilled and ackBracketMicros>0. Those fields come from the legacy successful click/authority-flip witnesses. C6 deliberately disables the old event4 flip and never sets flippedAt, so its four selected cuts cannot produce those required legacy values. The caller therefore fails cleanup before the new C6 producer seal/restoration retry can run.
findings.impact: All four C6 cases can reach genuine terminal outcomes yet fail fixture cleanup on inapplicable legacy witnesses. This also makes the retained guided restoration retry unreachable through shared cleanup.
findings.smallestFix: Add only a selected-C6 branch to the existing cleanup completion gate, reusing the actual C6 original-close/native-settlement/exact-restoration checks already provided by p8AwaitC6Closed. Preserve legacy residual-click/authority-flip requirements for non-C6 cases. Do not fabricate old residual/ACK values. Keep a failed-C6 teardown retry reachable separately from successful-completion predicates.

findings.title: Unconfirmed cleanup skips the retained guided restoration task
findings.sourceEvidence: A guided busy-drain timeout leaves revC6RetryRestore retained, and the existing seal-command watcher can invoke it. Java sends that command from p8C6Case finally only inside !cleanupUnconfirmed. p3Case sets cleanupUnconfirmed when original cleanup throws, including absent restoration/owner-close failure. On precisely that branch, outer finally emits only a cleanup failure and does not send the retry command. Residual process cleanup does not invoke the runtime retry either.
findings.impact: After a first bounded drain attempt expires, dispatch can subsequently settle while installed hooks/native wrappers remain retained in the live worker with no Java retry invocation. The source keeps a restoration capability but never uses it on the intended failure branch.
findings.smallestFix: Attempt the existing selected restoration command in outer finally independently of cleanupUnconfirmed, preserving the original failure and keeping capture/options tags until restoration is actually observed. Any producer failure/owner-close failure must remain sticky; a restoration attempt must not clear cleanupUnconfirmed, certify owner closure, or permit another case. The existing task must still wait for actual dispatch settlement before descriptor removal.

additionalChecks.assessment: Runtime validation failures remain sticky. Only an accepted selected-document focus-enter response IOException becomes provisional interruption, and the terminal helper requires actual native-pending receipt, original close, unavailable fence and UNKNOWN phase. This does not manufacture a healthy ACK or zero-effect proof.

The source now requires one actual RESOLVED dispatch RELEASE and one actual UNKNOWN_OUTCOME USAGE after cleanup, linked to the immutable release identifier and matching version/scope/accepted attempt or consumed admission via existing helpers. It preserves the forbidden positive/refusal/no-use usage checks. The assertions are scalar and do not print audit records. These source assertions remain unexecuted and are presently behind the cleanup blocker.

Root explicitly accepts selected page server focus ingress plus a contemporaneous original Node pending acknowledgement as entry proof. Page response completion during synchronous stall is not a prerequisite; unavailable final page fence remains UNKNOWN effect knowledge. No additional page-ACK requirement imposed.
